claims.text: Proxies of human difficulty are negatively correlated with LLM response correctness.
Scaled-up and shaped-up language models do not secure low-difficulty operating areas where errors are eliminated.
Scaling and shaping interventions replace task avoidance with a higher proportion of incorrect answers.
LLM task avoidance rates do not increase as instance difficulty increases.
Human oversight and supervision fail to compensate for increased LLM errors on high-difficulty questions.
Scaling-up and shaping-up LLMs increase stability across different natural phrasings of the same question.
Pockets of prompt sensitivity variability persist across difficulty levels despite scaling and shaping interventions.

evidence.description: Except for BLOOM on addition, high correlations were observed across all model families between correctness and proxies for human difficulty (Supplementary Table 8).

For the LLaMA family, no model achieves 60% correctness at the simplest difficulty level (discounting 25% random guess for science), and GPT-4 primarily increases performance on medium/high difficulty tasks without clear improvement for easy tasks.

Scaling analysis shows avoidance is significantly lower for shaped-up models compared to raw models, while incorrectness and the ratio of incorrectness over non-correct answers (i/(a+i)) increase substantially.
The percentage of avoidant answers rarely rises quicker than the percentage of incorrect ones across difficulty bins, showing weak or absent correlation between avoidance and difficulty.
Human survey S2 shows high proportions of incorrect-to-correct supervision errors, where human participants mistake incorrect model outputs for correct answers on difficult instances.
Shaped-up models (the last six GPT models and chat LLaMA models) exhibit higher prompting stability across 15 natural prompt variations relative to raw base models.
Disaggregated prompting analysis shows non-monotonic prompt performance across difficulty levels, with certain prompts yielding higher accuracy on hard items but failing on easy items.

methodologies.name: Multi-family LLM reliability evaluation framework
methodologies.description: Evaluated 32 language models across 3 model families (GPT, LLaMA, BLOOM) using 5 benchmarks categorized into 30 difficulty bins and 15 natural prompt variations per benchmark, scoring outputs into three categories (correct, incorrect, avoidant).
conditions: Logistic calibration to human failure probability

methodologies.name: Human perceptual and supervision studies (S1 and S2)
methodologies.description: Conducted two human subject studies to calibrate instance difficulty proxies against human performance expectations (S1) and measure human capability to supervise/verify model outputs across difficulty levels (S2).
conditions: Three-valued confusion matrix evaluating correct, incorrect, and avoidant outputs

limitations.text: Recruitment of participants for the human studies consisted mostly of non-experts, leading to high calibrated difficulty values for general population capability.
The sample of natural prompts lacked frequency data corresponding to real-world prompt occurrence distributions.
The study evaluated specific model trajectories, excluding LLMs that delegate tasks to external tools or employ external reasoning techniques.
RLHF alignment techniques weaken model calibration and self-confidence estimation.

future_work.text: Incorporate difficulty concordance optimization and human verification error reduction explicitly into the loss function during LLM training and shaping.
Construct larger, higher-quality datasets capturing human difficulty expectations and output supervision for training AI supervisors.
Design specialized domain LLMs with explicit reject options or couple them with external AI supervisors to promote task avoidance when uncertain.
